title: S033 — Full correctness gate and wall-clock performance validation
description: Establish whether the corrected event-driven Phase-A executor is both exactly equivalent to authoritative derivation and materially faster than the reset-scope baseline.
result_summary: HOLD. Correctness is clean and broad: 25,500 prefixes, 0 mismatches across Verrin, Ordos and the full S024 corpus (including the five previously failing topologies); determinism 20/20; branch-from-incremental 20/20. The corrected executor is exactly equivalent to authoritative derivation. BUT the wall-clock benefit is workload-dependent and currently insufficient: TARGET is slower than from-scratch at H=100-1000 and wins only on some H=10,000 workloads (up to 2.13x). Measured A/T: sparse 0.48/0.81/1.12, medium 0.44/0.61/0.58, dense 0.67/0.57/2.13. The reason is precise: buildModel(canon, prefix) is O(H) per prefix and dominates BOTH paths, so the worklist's excellent locality (0.03-5.89 nodes processed/step vs 14 model nodes = 0.2-42%) is swamped by model construction at small H. Correction to S030: the ~6% figure was a node-count metric; the end-to-end wall-clock picture is mixed. 'Materially incremental' holds for the algorithm, not for wall clock.
locality: worklist processes 0.03-5.89 nodes/step vs 14 model nodes (0.2-42%)
next_experiment: incrementalise buildModel itself (maintain the derivation model across prefixes by applying one intervention to the previous model instead of rebuilding from the full chain), then re-run the S033 three-way comparison.
limitations: Only Verrin used for the performance sweep (Ordos omitted for budget); correctness covers both canons.
